findings.title: Staging dir symlink/race in os.tmpdir
findings.disposition_rationale: mkdtempSync creates a 0700 owner-only staging dir; no other local user can create <staging>/<issue> inside it, so the predicted symlink race is unreachable. Standard secure-temp pattern used across the codebase.

findings.title: checkAnchorDir({}) scope leg / multi-issue fixture vacuity
findings.disposition_rationale: Primary claim false: the FAFF-1347 events_scope leg is always-on in validateAnchorDir (evidence.js:591 unconditionally validates events.jsonl scoped); {} does not disable it (verified: events_scope.scope==FAFF-A, out_of_scope_rows==1). Valid secondary point fixed: the multi-issue fixture now gives FAFF-B an evidence-invalid row that gates whole-file, so the exit-0 mint for FAFF-A proves scope narrowing non-vacuously.

findings.title: Exit 4 collides with commissaire admit exit 4
findings.disposition_rationale: Spec-closed decision (Chosen: 4). Both admit-4 and anchor-4 mean 'nothing written'; 4 is distinct from audit anchor's own usage(2)/no-events(3) so a schema refusal stays machine-distinguishable within the subcommand; no shared caller in-repo branches on the bare binary exit across subcommands.

findings.title: cpSync placement is not atomic (partial tree on mid-copy failure)
findings.disposition_rationale: Identical to today's mintIssueAnchor direct-write placement; a cpSync throw propagates to a non-zero exit, never a false exit 0. Spec explicitly rejected rename (EXDEV) and rmSync (destructive); atomic placement is named out-of-scope hardening. CI evidence-schema:require is the whole-tree backstop.
